definitions: A fleshy appendage of some seeds, typically formed from the funiculus, that may partially or completely enclose the seed.
An extra seed covering, typically colored and fleshy, that grows from the hilum or funiculus and is often edible.
examples: The bright red aril of the yew seed is poisonous.
Many tropical fruits have an edible aril.
The aril can aid in seed dispersal.
